# Return Objective: One-Page Summary (D12)
*As of 2026-10-19. Generated by `python run_all.py --only portfolio`. Values provisional (team, 2026-10-28).*

## 1. What the endowment needs
Required return = (1 + inflation)(1 + spending)(1 + real growth)(1 + costs) − 1 = (1 + 2.35%)(1 + 2.65%)(1 + 0.50%)(1 + 0.20%) − 1 = **5.80% per year**

| Input | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Inflation | 2.35% | FRED 10-year breakeven (market's expected US inflation); spending assumed in USD |
| Spending | 2.65% | Scholarships, research and other university needs |
| Real growth | 0.50% | Grow purchasing power slightly above inflation |
| Extra costs | 0.20% | Management and trading costs not already inside ETF prices |

## 2. What portfolios can realistically earn
Expected compound return = CAPM (risk-free 4.10% + β × equity risk premium 5%; AGG = its yield, D25) − ½ variance (daily-return covariance). Reference portfolios only; the optimised candidates come in the portfolio stage.

| Portfolio | Expected return | Volatility | Gap vs need | Meets need? | **Spending it can support** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Defensive 30/50/20 SPY/AGG/GLD | 5.44% | 7.7% | 0.36% | No | **2.30%** |
| 40/60 SPY/AGG | 5.81% | 8.2% | -0.01% | Yes | **2.66%** |
| 60/40 SPY/AGG | 6.47% | 11.5% | -0.67% | Yes | **3.30%** |
| Equal weight 7 | 6.63% | 15.8% | -0.83% | Yes | **3.46%** |

## 3. What this means for the committee
- 1 of 4 reference portfolios fall short of the 5.80% requirement at a 5% equity premium.
- **Agreed shortfall policy: lower spending, not more risk.** The most defensive mix (Defensive 30/50/20 SPY/AGG/GLD) supports about **2.30% spending** instead of 2.65%; Equal weight 7 supports about 3.46%, but with 15.8% volatility.
- "Spending it can support" keeps inflation protection, 0.50% real growth and 0.20% costs, and solves for the spending rate that makes expected return equal to the requirement.

## 5. Caveats
- Own-data equity premium is 9.7% (95% CI 3.5%–15.8%). 2004–2026 was unusually strong for US stocks, so a 5% base is used.
- CAPM gives gold about 4.6% (β ≈ 0) against 10.3% historically; it ignores gold's role as an inflation and crisis hedge.
- Base case uses today's T-bill (4.10%). If short rates average less over 5 years, every CAPM expected return falls one-for-one (table above). AGG's real sensitivity is smaller because its current yield is locked in for its ~6-year duration.
- Tax-exempt base case. Withholding is applied per ETF on each fund's own distribution yield: 30% on equity ETFs, AGG interest exempt: −0.09% to −0.37%; 30% on all distributions (upper bound): −0.55% to −0.87%.
- Variance drag uses daily-return covariance (60/40: ~11.5% volatility). Monthly data gives lower volatility (~9.4%) and would flatter compound returns; monthly figures are reported for information only.
- Gold's protective value is assessed separately (research doc §7), not through CAPM.
- Expected returns are estimates with wide uncertainty; the risk stage tests downside, which matters more for this client.
